_format.description: Exemplar input for the DAGGER Visualizer (https://knyarko.github.io/DAGGER_Visualizer/). Mirrors the {nodes, edges} dual-array shape: each `nodes` row is a fact triple (subject → predicate → object) with rich attributes; each `edges` row is a directed link between two node ids. The visualizer flattens nested fields and lets the user pick which array to render and which columns drive source/target/color/size/label.

nodes.label: Spearphishing email delivery
nodes.info: Adversary sends a tailored email to Finance staff with a weaponised Excel attachment.
nodes.subject: Adversary
nodes.text_msg: Subject: 'Q1 invoice reconciliation' — sender domain spoofs vendor 'acmesupply.com'.
nodes.triplet_justification: Email headers and link patterns match the actor's known phishing infrastructure; first observed in similar campaigns Feb 2026.

nodes.label: User opens malicious attachment
nodes.info: Finance user double-clicks the Excel file; macros prompt is dismissed and content runs.
nodes.subject: Finance user
nodes.text_msg: User reported opening attachment shortly before EDR alert fired.
nodes.triplet_justification: EDR process tree shows EXCEL.EXE spawning a child PowerShell within 4 seconds of file open.

nodes.label: PowerShell loader runs
nodes.info: Macro launches an obfuscated PowerShell command that fetches a second-stage payload.
nodes.subject: PowerShell loader
nodes.triplet_justification: Encoded PowerShell with web download is the most common second-stage delivery pattern; matches the actor's TTPs.
nodes.all_info: Command-line interpreter abuse — see ATT&CK T1059.001.

nodes.label: Beacon implant deployed
nodes.info: Second-stage downloads a Cobalt-Strike-style beacon binary into %APPDATA%.
nodes.subject: Stage-two loader
nodes.triplet_justification: Hash matches a Cobalt-Strike beacon variant first reported by CrowdStrike in 2025-Q4.

nodes.label: Registry Run-Key persistence
nodes.info: Beacon writes itself into HKCU Run for survival across reboots.
nodes.subject: Beacon implant
nodes.triplet_justification: Standard persistence pattern documented in MITRE ATT&CK T1547.001.

nodes.label: Process injection into lsass.exe
nodes.info: Beacon reflectively loads code into lsass to read credential material.
nodes.subject: Beacon implant
nodes.text_msg: EDR flagged unsigned thread starting in lsass.exe owned by SYSTEM.
nodes.triplet_justification: Reflective injection into lsass is a classic credential-access enabler; correlates with subsequent NTLM hashes seen on wire.

nodes.label: Credentials extracted from LSASS
nodes.info: NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets harvested for several domain users.
nodes.subject: Adversary
nodes.text_msg: Tools resembling mimikatz' sekurlsa::logonpasswords output observed in beacon memory.
nodes.triplet_justification: Memory artefacts match known mimikatz strings; subsequent lateral moves used pass-the-hash.

nodes.label: AD enumeration via LDAP queries
nodes.info: Beacon queries Active Directory for high-value groups (Domain Admins, Server Admins).
nodes.subject: Beacon implant
nodes.text_msg: LDAP search filter '(memberOf=CN=Domain Admins,...)' originated from finance workstation.
nodes.triplet_justification: Pattern of high-cardinality LDAP queries from a non-IT host is a strong recon indicator.

nodes.label: Domain Controllers identified
nodes.info: Adversary maps DC1.corp.local and DC2.corp.local from LDAP responses.
nodes.subject: Adversary
nodes.text_msg: Internal log captured outbound LDAP-search responses listing both DCs.
nodes.triplet_justification: Direct result of the LDAP enumeration in ATK008; sets up the subsequent ransomware staging.

nodes.label: Lateral movement via RDP
nodes.info: Adversary uses pass-the-hash to RDP into a server in the IT subnet.
nodes.subject: Adversary
nodes.text_msg: RDP session opened from finance host to SRV-IT-04 using compromised local-admin hash.
nodes.triplet_justification: Source/destination pair and Kerberos ticket reuse confirm pass-the-hash technique.

nodes.label: C2 channel established over HTTPS
nodes.info: Beacon dials home to attacker infrastructure using HTTPS to look like normal traffic.
nodes.subject: Beacon implant
nodes.text_msg: Outbound HTTPS to cdn-mirror.example[.]com on port 443 with self-signed cert; jitter ~30s.
nodes.triplet_justification: Domain registration date (5 days prior to incident) and beacon timing match the actor's known C2 fingerprint.

nodes.label: Exfiltration of credentials
nodes.info: Stolen NTLM hashes and AD enumeration data exfiltrated via the established C2 channel.
nodes.subject: C2 channel
nodes.text_msg: PCAP shows ~12KB encrypted POST bodies to C2 domain immediately after credential dump.
nodes.triplet_justification: Volume and timing of POST bodies correlate with the LSASS dump completion.

nodes.label: Ransomware payload deployed
nodes.info: Adversary stages ransomware binary on file server and uses GPO to push to endpoints.
nodes.subject: Adversary
nodes.text_msg: New GPO 'WindowsSecurityUpdate' assigned a startup script pointing to \\SRV-IT-04\share$\update.exe.
nodes.triplet_justification: GPO modification and binary staging are the staging vector for the Akira-family ransomware variant observed.

nodes.label: Production file shares encrypted
nodes.info: Endpoints execute ransomware at next reboot; ~12 TB across shares are encrypted.
nodes.subject: Ransomware payload
nodes.text_msg: Files renamed with .akira extension; ransom note 'akira_readme.txt' dropped in each directory.
nodes.triplet_justification: Extension and ransom-note pattern map to the Akira ransomware family.

nodes.label: Business operations halted
nodes.info: Finance, payroll, and ticketing applications all dependent on the encrypted shares; operations stop.
nodes.subject: Encrypted file shares
nodes.text_msg: Helpdesk receives surge of 'cannot open file' tickets across departments; SAP and AP/AR offline.
nodes.triplet_justification: Direct downstream effect of share encryption; reported in incident post-mortem.

nodes.label: Initial Access
nodes.info: MITRE ATT&CK tactic — adversary gains foothold in the network.

nodes.label: Execution
nodes.info: MITRE ATT&CK tactic — adversary-controlled code runs on a local or remote system.

nodes.label: Persistence
nodes.info: MITRE ATT&CK tactic — maintain foothold across restarts, credential changes, or interruptions.

nodes.label: Defense Evasion
nodes.info: MITRE ATT&CK tactic — avoid detection by EDR / antivirus / logging.

nodes.label: Credential Access
nodes.info: MITRE ATT&CK tactic — steal account names and passwords.

nodes.label: Discovery
nodes.info: MITRE ATT&CK tactic — gain knowledge of the environment.

nodes.label: Lateral Movement
nodes.info: MITRE ATT&CK tactic — move through the environment to reach the objective.

nodes.label: Command and Control
nodes.info: MITRE ATT&CK tactic — communicate with compromised systems to control them.

nodes.label: Impact
nodes.info: MITRE ATT&CK tactic — destroy, expose, or disrupt the target's data and systems.
